overview.body:
**Onuris** ​(*onuris*) — ‌He Who ‌Brings Back ​the ​Distant One ​· He ​who ​brings back ‌the distant ​one — ​belongs ‌to the ​Egyptian tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued under ​the domain ​"War, ​Hunting". The ​name means ​"He ‌who brings ​back the ‌distant one"[^1].

​**ꜥnḥ ‌wr** — ​Onuris — ‌is ​the god ‌of the ​retrieved: the ​spear-carrying ‌hunter who ‌fetches back ‌the ​goddess who ​fled. His ‌myth is ​the ​cosmic courtship ‌of the ​runaway ​lioness Mehyt, ‌brought home ​from the ‌Nubian ​hills to ​This; his ​cult ​was the ‌war-cult of ‌the Thinite ​nome, ‌the kings’ ​ancestral land.[^2]

​PuniCodex ‌restores the ‌name as ‌**Onuris** and ‌serves ​its temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/onuris/). ​The restoration ​aSCII-equivalent form ‌— a ​description ​computed from ​the displayed ‌form ​itself. The ​plain ASCII ​form *onuris* ‌survives ​as a ‌modern convenience ​imposed ‌by the ​early domain-name ‌system; the ‌restoration, ​not the ​fallback, is ​the ​form the ‌project defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^3].

the-name.body:
The ​name ‌is attested ‌in ​Egyptian ​hieroglyphs ​as ​**𓏎𓈖𓁷𓂋𓏏𓈐𓅆**. Etymologically ​it ‌means ​"He ​who brings ‌back ​the ‌distant ​one"[^1].

The ‌ASCII ​form ​*onuris* ​survives ​only because ​the ‌early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not ‌carry ​diacritics; ‌it ​is a ‌technological ​compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ‌spelling. ‌The ​Unicode ​restoration **Onuris** ‌recovers ​the ​full ‌diacritic ​detail of ​the ‌scholarly ​transliteration ‌directly in ​the ​address ​bar. ​The ‌restoration aSCII-equivalent ‌form ​— ‌a ​description computed ​from ‌the ‌displayed ‌form itself.

‌The ​letter-by-letter ‌transformation ​runs:

- ​**o** → ​**O** ‌— ​Same, ​capitalized
- **n** ​→ ‌**n** ​— ​Same
- ​**u** → ‌**u** ​— ‌Same
- ​**r** → ‌**r** ​— ‌Same
- ‌**i** → ​**i** ​— ​Same
- ​**s** ‌→ **s** ‌— ​Same

domains.body:
**ꜥnḥ ​wr** — ‌Onuris ‌— is ​the ​god of ​the ​retrieved: the ​spear-carrying ‌hunter who ​fetches ​back the ‌goddess ​who fled. ‌His ​myth is ‌the ​cosmic courtship ​of ​the runaway ​lioness ​Mehyt, brought ‌home ​from the ‌Nubian ​hills to ‌This; ​his cult ‌was ​the war-cult ‌of ​the Thinite ​nome, ‌the kings’ ‌ancestral ‌land.[^1]

### The ​Retriever

​His name ‌is ​his mission: ​he ‌brings back ​the ​distant one ‌— ​the Eye ‌of ​Ra, the ​lioness, ​the runaway ​glory.

### ‌The Spear-Bearer

‌Armed ​with spear ‌and ​rope, the ​hunter ‌of the ‌high ‌desert; a ‌war-god ​of the ‌oldest ​royal nome.

### ​Husband ​of Mehyt

‌His ​consort is ​the ​fierce lioness ‌Mehyt ​— the ​retrieved ​Eye, tamed ‌by ​marriage, not ‌chains.

### ​Lord of ‌This

​His city, ‌This ‌(Girga), stood ​beside ​Abydos — ​the ​ancestral seat ‌of ‌the first ​dynasties.

symbols.body:
The ​iconography ‌associated ‌with Onuris ​concentrates ​in ​a ​small ​set ‌of recurring ​attributes, ​each ‌a ​compressed ‌statement ​about the ‌name:[^1]

- ​**The ​Retriever** ​— ​His ​name is ‌his ​mission: ‌he ​brings ‌back the ​distant ‌one ​— ‌the ​Eye ​of Ra, ‌the ‌lioness, ‌the ​runaway ​glory.
- ‌**The Spear-Bearer** ​— ​Armed ‌with ​spear ​and ‌rope, the ​hunter ‌of ​the ​high ​desert; ​a war-god ‌of ‌the ​oldest ‌royal ​nome.
- ​**Husband of ‌Mehyt** ‌— ‌His ‌consort ​is ‌the fierce ​lioness ​Mehyt ​— ‌the ​retrieved Eye, ​tamed ​by ‌marriage, ​not ​chains.
- ​**Lord of ‌This** ​— ‌His ​city, ‌This ​(Girga), stood ‌beside ‌Abydos ​— ​the ​ancestral ​seat of ‌the ‌first ​dynasties.

mythology.body:
Onuris’ mythology ​is the romance ‌of retrieval: the Eye ‌of Ra, in ​her lioness form ​as Mehyt, raged ​in the southern ​hills, and Onuris went ​up with spear ‌and rope and ​brought her home. ​The New Kingdom ‌theologians read the story ​as the sun’s ‌power recovered from ​the desert’s edge ‌— and as the ​model of the ​husband who fetches ​back what the ​household loses.[^1]

### The ​Fetching of the Lioness ‌(Thinite Tradition)

In ​the nome of ‌This the story ​ran: Mehyt, the lioness, ‌fled into the ​eastern hills; Onuris ‌pursued, threw the ​rope, and brought ‌her down — and ​married her. The ​temple hymns celebrate ‌the return procession: ‌the retrieved goddess ‌re-entering the town at ​her husband’s side, ​the desert’s ferocity ‌domesticated into civic ​power.[^2]

### The Solar Eye ​Recovered (Eye of ‌Ra Cycle)

Read ​cosmically, Onuris’ retrieval ​is Shu’s embassy ‌to the Eye — ​the same story ‌the Leiden hymns ​tell of Tefnut’s ​return. Onuris is ​Shu’s local, warlike face: ​the one god ‌whose job description ‌is fetching the ​godhead’s missing power, whether ‌by flattery or ​by spear.

### The ​God of the ‌First Nome (Royal ‌Ancestry)

This and Abydos ‌were the ground ‌of the first ​kings; Onuris received ‌the devotion of ​dynasties that claimed the ​Thinite soil as ​their own. His ‌was the war-god ​of the ancestral nome ​— the spear ​at the head ‌of the line ​that unified the ​Two Lands.

### Onuris-Shu of ​the Sky (Late ‌Theology)

In the ​Late Period he ‌was fully identified with ​Shu, the air ‌that holds up ​the sky — ‌the retriever who ‌brings back Nut herself ​each dawn. The ​lioness he fetched ​became the sky’s ​ferocity, and his ‌spear the axis that ‌keeps the vault ​in place.
